project_overview: The codebase appears to be a component-heavy Vue-based front-end application, likely managing student/application processes given the naming conventions (ExamFormSubmission, HallTicketPage). The dependency structure is implicit, relying heavily on component composition, suggesting a component-centric architecture. The identified issues point to localized complexity hot spots within specific transactional views, indicating potential difficulties in state management or lifecycle handling.

layers.description: This layer constitutes the vast majority of files, composed of Vue components responsible for UI rendering and user interaction. These components handle presentation logic and assemble the final user experience. Examples include views for dashboards, forms, and dedicated informational pages.

macro_trends.title: High Component Complexity Concentration (God Components)
macro_trends.description: Several specific views are flagged with multiple unresolved issues, suggesting they are acting as 'God Components' or architectural hubs that are over-encapsulating too much state or logic. Specifically, 'SelectedApplicationService.vue' reports 5 issues, and 'ExamFormSubmission.vue' reports 3 issues, pointing to deeply coupled state logic or excessive lifecycle management within these single files. This violates Single Responsibility Principle (SRP).

macro_trends.title: Potential Prop-Drilling/State Incoherence Risk
macro_trends.description: Given the numerous, specialized, and process-oriented views (e.g., 'ExamFormSubmission.vue' communicating with 'FeeDetails.vue' implicitly), there is a high risk of prop-drilling or localized state mismanagement. Without explicit dependency arrows, the sheer number of transactional components suggests state might be passed deep down the component tree rather than centralized via a dedicated store (Pinia/Vuex).

macro_trends.title: Lack of Separation Between Core Views and Utilities
macro_trends.description: All provided files reside in a single conceptual grouping (implied by the common path structure), leading to an apparent conflation of concerns. There is no discernible separation between highly reusable, low-level utility modules (e.g., `apiClient.js`, `utils.js`) and the high-level presentation components. This increases the risk of 'Cross-Layer Contamination' if utility functions start importing component-specific context.

key_workflows.name: Application Lifecycle Management
key_workflows.description: This critical path likely flows through 'defaultLayout.vue' (id: 1) as the root container, coordinating between 'ApplicationServices.vue' (id: 2) and potentially 'ExamFormSubmission.vue' (id: 3). The dependency flow is sequential: User lands -> interacts with services/forms -> state updates must persist across these views. The high issue count on these initial/service components suggests the transactional state management is the primary point of failure or fragility.

key_workflows.name: Resource Upload and View Finalization
key_workflows.description: This workflow involves component interactions such as 'uploadFile.vue' (id: 14) and 'uploadProgessFile.vue' (id: 15), which feed into finalized results displayed on 'ResultPage.vue' (id: 11) or 'HallTicketPage.vue' (id: 5). The coupling here is structural: the success of the final view depends on the correct, immutable state propagated from these utility-like upload components.
